findings.statement: MUST FIX: the immutable authority-snapshot loader is schema fail-open. _authority_registry constructs an AuthorityRegistry for every YAML mapping and invokes _validate_authority_snapshot only when payload.schema already equals htt.pr122.authority_snapshot.v1; a missing, misspelled, or attacker-selected schema therefore bypasses every snapshot_status, immutable, exact-principal, exact-role/scope, selected-row-hash, and snapshot-registry-ref check. The only production call site supplies DEFAULT_AUTHORITY, so there is no declared alternate schema that justifies this fallback. This violates the spec's exact immutable snapshot contract even though the current checked-in snapshot passes.
assumptions_used: docs/research_program/long_horizon_rescue/pr122_spec.yaml:372-382 makes htt.pr122.authority_snapshot.v1 the exact PR-122 authority input contract.
The targeted call-site search is complete within the declared builder input and shows _authority_registry is used only for the PR-122 authority_path.
Unknown or unverified inputs must reject or block, per pr122_spec.yaml:120-141.
counterevidence_refs: scripts/codex_harness/build_claim_evidence_graph.py:445-509 thoroughly validates the snapshot after the conditional branch selects it.
The current targeted suite passed 29/29; that confirms current-fixture behavior, not unknown-schema rejection.
reproduction: Inspect lines 416-442: change payload.schema to any value other than htt.pr122.authority_snapshot.v1; control flow skips _validate_authority_snapshot and returns the generic registry.
Run the declared test-coverage rg command; none of the three declared test files contains an unknown/missing authority-snapshot schema mutation.
Patch by requiring payload.get('schema') == 'htt.pr122.authority_snapshot.v1' unconditionally before constructing or returning the registry, then always call _validate_authority_snapshot.
Add a regression test that mutates/removes schema while keeping principal rows otherwise constructible and asserts rejection before graph or receipt production.
unresolved: Keep PR-122 and G-PR122-FINAL-CONSUMERS open until the fail-open branch and its mutation test are fixed.
After the patch, regenerate the content-addressed graph, receipts, manifest, and literal pin because the builder source hash is graph-bound, then rerun exact consumer checks.

findings.statement: STEELMAN / FIXED-POINT REVIEW: apart from F-PR122-CODE-001, the design is internally coherent and materially stronger than a boolean readiness gate. Nodes, edges, closures, test executions, receipts, verifier semantics, and lineage are canonical content addresses; every direct claim producer must own an input/config/environment/check chain; test authority is derived from exact collected/executed/outcome identities; invalid/stale/missing evidence outranks an expected policy block; the literal-only pin is parsed without execution and breaks the verifier-to-graph cycle; consumers rehash graph sources, MES consumers, manifest inputs/artifacts, and exact closure/receipt axes while preserving claim_release_allowed=false.
assumptions_used: The checked-in literal pin is the commit-reviewed process trust root described by frozen decision D-PIN-LITERAL.
This verdict is about C1 mechanics only and does not promote scientific status or validate an estimand.
counterevidence_refs: The literal pin remains a manually reviewed trust root outside the graph and must be regenerated after any graph-bound source change.
The v2 acceptance lock is explicitly post-implementation, not prospective preregistration.
reproduction: Targeted authority, closure, lineage, and release-binding checks passed as part of 29 passed in 5.02s.
Kill switch: any graph/source/receipt/manifest/pin mismatch or any blocked-plus-invalid evidence state must stop consumer production.
unresolved: Residual process risk remains concentrated in commit review of the literal pin and immutable snapshot provenance; neither is independent scientific authority.

findings.statement: CACHE-AUTHORITY / REGRESSION REVIEW: the CF4 reviewed-binary pin optimization is build-local rather than module-global. _entry_rows loads one validated snapshot, reuses only its typed pin mapping, rehashes the policy before returning, and build_zip_bytes re-reads every source and verifies bytes, hashes, content mode, and binary binding before opening the ZIP writer. The dedicated call-count test passed. This preserves authority while removing repeated policy parsing.
assumptions_used: Package construction remains single-process and uses the returned rows without caller mutation.
Repository-wide quarantine validation remains the final pre-ZIP gate.
counterevidence_refs: A concurrent policy mutation after _entry_rows returns is not directly exercised by the call-count test, although later source-byte, binary-binding, and repository quarantine checks remain fail-closed.
reproduction: If cache scope is widened beyond one _entry_rows call, require a new mutation test that changes policy bytes between payload and archive construction.
unresolved: Follow-up only: add an explicit between-payload-and-ZIP policy-race test if multi-process or long-lived package builders are introduced.

findings.title: Installer now preserves or refuses divergent merge-only policy assets before its first destination write
findings.evidence: Every AGENTS/agent/.codex merge-only destination is preflighted for symlinks, non-regular files, and byte divergence before mkdir/copy begins. Missing files are copied, identical files are retained, and divergent AGENTS.md or .codex/config.toml causes exit 1 without creating agent.md or changing either local file. The clean install, clean reinstall, contaminated-vendor refusal, and two existing-target conflict paths passed in the targeted run.
findings.test_outcome: 3 passed within the combined 7 passed in 1.70s
findings.remaining_risk: The focused regression exercises divergent regular files, not a destination symlink; symlink refusal is established by direct source inspection. A failure in a validator that runs after non-merge-only copying is not transactionally rolled back, but that is outside the destructive merge-only overwrite defect closed here.

findings.title: SubagentStop, harness validation, and result merge reject unregistered or malformed handoffs
findings.evidence: The stop hook resolves ACTIVE_RUN, requires a regular registered assignment, validates its schema/context/canonical result path, rejects escaping or mismatched paths, validates the result payload, and binds marker status to artifact status. The shared validator and merger reuse the same assignment/result validators. The targeted fixture accepted one valid registered envelope and blocked a missing marker, an unregistered assignment, an empty result object, a status mismatch, and an unsafe identifier.
findings.test_outcome: 1 passed within the combined 7 passed in 1.70s; PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 .agent-harness/scripts/validate_harness.py returned ok=true for active_run=pr122-final-review-20260716
findings.remaining_risk: The unit fixture invokes the stop-hook program directly rather than through a live Codex lifecycle event; the assignment-binding and fail-closed payload semantics themselves are exercised.

findings.title: Reviewed-binary policy authority is build-local, immutable, rehashed, and covered by an actual byte-drift mutation
findings.evidence: ReviewedActiveBinaryPinSnapshot explicitly has no module-global cache; its pin map is wrapped in MappingProxyType, and the canonical policy bytes are re-read and SHA-256 compared before the snapshot is accepted as current. The new mutation test changes the policy bytes observed at the recheck and proves fail-closed CF4P0PolicyError behavior. The immutable-map, stale-digest, current-policy, and actual-byte-drift paths all passed.
findings.test_outcome: 2 passed within the combined 7 passed in 1.70s
findings.remaining_risk: This mutation is injected at the policy-byte reader boundary; it does not schedule a real concurrent filesystem writer. The trust-relevant changed-byte condition and rejection branch are nevertheless exact.

findings.title: The merge path preserves distinct raw findings and rejects malformed independent envelopes
findings.evidence: Independent result validation requires a nonempty evidence_fingerprint for every finding. The canonical-key fallback also includes finding_id when a malformed finding lacks a fingerprint, so malformed HARN-001 and HARN-002 records cannot collapse before rejection. The current merged artifact reports result_count=3, raw_finding_count=13, unique_finding_count=13, duplicate_count=1 for every retained finding, 13 distinct finding IDs/fingerprints, and errors=[].
findings.reproduction: PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 venv/bin/python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider -q scripts/codex_harness/test_codex_assets.py::test_shared_context_result_merge_never_collapses_missing_fingerprints; then parse .agent-harness/runs/pr122-final-review-20260716/MERGED_RESULTS.json and assert raw_finding_count == unique_finding_count == len(findings) == 13, all finding_id and evidence_fingerprint values are unique, all duplicate_count values equal 1, and errors == []
findings.test_outcome: The canonical-key regression passed; the declared merged snapshot satisfies the complete 13-of-13 preservation invariant
findings.remaining_risk: MERGED_RESULTS.json predates this recheck envelope. The main writer must rerun merge_results.py after all final-review results are present and verify that the original 13 finding IDs remain a subset; the expected total will then exceed 13.

findings.title: Installer overwrites existing repository policy and intentional Codex configuration
findings.evidence: INSTALL_NOTES.md and .agent-harness/README.md require merging AGENTS.md.fragment and .codex/config.toml, and config.toml itself warns not to overwrite intentional settings. scripts/install_codex_handoff.sh instead copies AGENTS.md and all .codex assets directly over the target. A focused temporary-target probe returned agents_preserved=false and config_preserved=false. The installer test creates an empty target, so it cannot detect this destructive upgrade-path behavior.
findings.impact: Installing or upgrading the harness in a real repository can silently erase durable operating policy and model/provider configuration before validation runs; a later validator failure also leaves a partially overwritten target.
findings.remediation: Implement an explicit merge-or-refuse transaction: preserve an existing AGENTS.md and config.toml, append/merge only missing harness keys/fragment after conflict checks, stage into a temporary tree, validate, then atomically promote. Add an existing-target preservation/conflict test.

findings.title: SubagentStop accepts an unregistered assignment with an empty result object
findings.evidence: The accepted-path fixture in scripts/codex_harness/test_codex_assets.py creates ACTIVE_RUN, CONTEXT_INDEX.json, and a result file containing only {}, but creates no assignment JSON; it then expects the stop hook to accept silently. A focused execution reproduced acceptance for that unregistered empty result, while invalid status and stale context were correctly blocked.
findings.impact: A subagent can stop successfully without the registered Tier-1 assignment or schema-valid evidence envelope, contradicting the mandatory handoff contract and G-HARNESS-INSTALL's invalid-result fail condition. Later merge validation is too late to make SubagentStop fail closed.
findings.remediation: At SubagentStop, resolve ACTIVE_RUN, require the registered assignment file, bind assignment_id/context_version/result_path/independence_mode to it, parse the result JSON against the result-envelope schema, and reject missing required evidence fields. Replace the current accepted fixture with a real minimal valid assignment and envelope, plus negative unregistered/empty/path-traversal tests.

findings.remediation: Regenerate the canonical CF4 inventory and dependent block through the authorized PR-120 generator, review the resulting diff, then rerun the quarantine and audit-package dry-run/check gates.

findings.title: Codex hook/config compatibility coverage is structural but not end-to-end
findings.evidence: test_shared_context_packet_is_merged_and_versioned checks only the hook event-name set. The custom config validator checks a local allowlist but does not validate hooks.json. SessionStart and SubagentStart are not executed in the declared asset test; only SubagentStop is invoked directly. Local Codex 0.144.4 does report hooks as stable and loads the current project config, so this is a coverage gap rather than evidence of incompatibility.
findings.impact: Matcher, command, timeout, trust, and injection regressions can pass the asset suite even when the live Codex hook path is broken.
findings.remediation: Add a Codex-version-pinned hook schema/doctor check and isolated SessionStart/SubagentStart integration fixtures that assert exact injected context and stale/missing assignment behavior.

findings.title: Performance safeguards lack adversarial state-change tests
findings.evidence: The new test proves one snapshot and one final policy recheck, but does not mutate policy/sidecar state between those points. The lru_cache tests document read-only use but do not assert that cached helpers are never consumed by a repository-mutating test.
findings.impact: Future refactors could broaden cache scope or weaken the build-local recheck without a targeted test failing.
findings.remediation: Add a temporary-repository mutation test showing policy drift is rejected after row construction and retain explicit cache-clear/fresh-process tests for mutation lanes.

The roadmap requires both PR3 and PR4 ensembles, a PR4 download, a PR4 size-probe decision, PR4 null analysis, and a combined C3 output; it explicitly says PR4 is mandatory, not optional.

CLAIM_LEDGER.md:9 instead records Owner as COMMON/HTT.
The roadmap at lines 110-112 requires one canonical owner and separate contributors/adjudicator/implementation scope.

findings.title: Claim ledger publishes an unbound 195-test integration count
evidence: CLAIM_LEDGER.md:9 cites a 132-test authoritative receipt and a 195-test consumer integration count without a path/hash/selector/environment receipt for the latter.
pr122_claim_closure_report.json:325-608 binds only the 132 collected and 132 executed authoritative receipt.
findings.consequence: The additional count is not reproducibly attributable from the assignment-declared evidence and can drift independently of the content-addressed graph.
findings.required_resolution: Either bind the 195-test suite to an exact execution receipt with selector/environment hashes or remove the count and cite the reproducible check command without a manual number.

findings.title: Publication freeze labels roadmap C-levels as Tier without distinguishing canonical ClaimTier
evidence: publication_claim_freeze.md:3-8 gives the artifact canonical claim_tier diagnostic_only, while the table at lines 103-114 uses a column named Tier containing C1-C4 roadmap levels.
The roadmap at lines 66-76 explicitly says the C0-C6 ladder and canonical ClaimTier are not one ordered enum.
findings.consequence: Readers can mistake scientific level C2/C4 for canonical conditional/validated status even though caveats correctly downclaim the rows.
findings.required_resolution: Rename the table column to Scientific level and, where material, add a separate canonical ClaimTier column.
